candidate.answerReason: The only triples are (2004,1,0) and (1002,1002,1). For c at least 2, the logarithmic equation forces b to exceed 2005.

methods.label: Separate the small values of c
methods.explanation:
The logarithmic equation becomes more useful in exponential form. Since \(a\ge2\) and \(b\ge1\), the logarithm is defined, and
\[
\log_a b=c^{2005}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
b=a^{c^{2005}}.
\]
The nonnegative integer \(c\) is either \(0\), \(1\), or at least \(2\).

If \(c=0\), then \(b=a^0=1\). The sum condition gives \(a+1=2005\), producing the valid triple \((2004,1,0)\).

If \(c=1\), then \(b=a\). Thus \(2a+1=2005\), producing the valid triple \((1002,1002,1)\).

If \(c\ge2\), then \(c^{2005}\ge2^{2005}>11\). Since \(a\ge2\), this forces
\[
b=a^{c^{2005}}\ge2^{11}=2048>2005.
\]
That is impossible when \(a+b+c=2005\) and all three summands are nonnegative.

These cases cover every allowed integer \(c\), and each of the first two cases gives exactly one triple. Therefore there are \(\boxed{2}\) triples, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
